requirement: Line-hit result does not imply every statement executed

obligations.note: all three semicolon-joined statements complete; ground truth for which ones is the log side-channel, not this obligation alone

reached, and the first statement (log.append("first")) completes; the second statement (100 / divisor) raises a runtime division-by-zero error mid-evaluation, aborting the line before the third statement (log.append("second")) ever runs. A line-granularity tool can only report this line as hit=true either way -- it cannot express that two of the three statements on it did not finish. The log array is the actual ground truth for that finer-grained fact; this obligation alone is NOT sufficient to distinguish this input from all_complete, and is not meant to be -- see notes.
never reached: the function aborts on line 4's error before returning

notes: GDScript allows semicolon-separated simple statements on one physical line (confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine). This fixture's line-4 obligation is deliberately identical (hit=true) across both inputs -- that IS the point being demonstrated, not an oversight: a line-granularity coverage schema genuinely cannot discriminate 'all three statements ran' from 'only the first one did' using hits alone, since both produce the same single line-hit fact. The `expected_log` field carries the actual finer-grained ground truth (which statements ran, via an explicit log.append() side-channel each statement performs), the same technique used in F030 to make short-circuit evaluation observable where a boolean return value alone would be insufficient. `expected_log` is fixture-specific, not part of the general Obligation schema, and is checked directly by pilot/fixtures/driver.gd rather than by pilot/harness/comparator.py.

ambiguities: A real coverage tool with only line-granularity hits (which is what most GDScript tools, including gd-tools 0.4.0, provide) has no way to surface the finer-grained fact this fixture documents at all -- there is no statement-level obligation kind in the schema to bind a 'partial line' report to. This fixture records the gap; closing it would require extending the schema with a statement-index concept, out of scope here.
